Congenital titin myopathy causes weakness and contractures; structural heart disease or cardiomyopathy affects roughly 40% of congenital titinopathy cohorts.

Congenital structural defect of the inferior eyelid; associated facial clefts or syndromes are not intrinsic to every case.
Neoplasm of the hair follicle infundibulum, a cutaneous appendage.
Hereditary optic nerve degeneration with visual loss; additional neurologic manifestations are occasional, 5-29%, below threshold.
Marrow myelodysplasia with monosomy 7 and frequent AML; no defining extrahematologic organ damage is documented.
Microcephaly and corpus callosum dysgenesis define brain involvement; cleft lip/palate defines an oral structural defect.
Primitive germ cell malignancy arises in the ovary as a reproductive organ; endocrine tissue origin or hormonal dysfunction is not defining.
Pheochromocytoma and pancreatic islet-cell tumors define endocrine involvement. Frequencies of cardiovascular injury are unspecified; episodic hypertension alone does not establish damage.
Hereditary neoplastic susceptibility specifically targets the lung; this primary label identifies the target organ, without implying established cancer or lung damage.
Primary bladder adenocarcinoma with colonic-type histology; urinary bladder origin determines the axis, without implying intestinal involvement.
